clue.text: Accurately reproduced version of Largo, conflated with hip-hop act

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged
things conflated are fused and jumbled together, a second signal that these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, hyphen ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician's take on a Largo has been blended with a hip-hop act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' and 'conflated' both signal the anagram of LARGO, HIPHOP and ACT, fourteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something photographical is rendered with the exact fidelity of a photograph, hence faithfully copied.

clue.text: Devise beliefs about silver brooms in 27

parts.note: to devise a scheme is to plan it

indicators.note: beliefs placed about silver means the word for beliefs is wrapped around it

parts.note: tenets are beliefs or principles
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone forms beliefs about silver brooms in a historic conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal house took its name from the broom plant, planta genista, worn as a badge; 27 is the Wars of the Roses, in which they fought.
explanation.definitionFit: The dynasty's name comes from planta genista, Latin for broom, so its members are punningly the brooms of the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Sink number coming up in the first place

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to sink a ball in snooker is to pot it

explanation.surface: A kitchen sink numbered first in a list of fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top means leading or ahead, the same idea as being in first position.

clue.text: 12 emblem rendered differently

indicators.note: rendered here means made into something else, so the letters of the emblem are rearranged

parts.note: 12 is the Yorkist side, whose badge was the white rose

explanation.surface: A partisan's badge is drawn in another style.
explanation.walkthrough: The white rose of York is the emblem; 'rendered' rearranges WHITEROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in another way, a straightforward synonym for differently.

clue.text: Emblem of 16 moved altar back

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so the letters of the emblem are rearranged

parts.note: 16 is the Lancaster side, whose badge was the red rose

explanation.surface: A family badge has been shifted to the back of a church altar.
explanation.walkthrough: The red rose of Lancaster is the emblem; 'moved' rearranges REDROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen standing behind a church altar.

clue.text: Syrian girlfriend produces toddy

definitions.meaning: an ancient city in Syria, playfully read as a pal called Myra
a tropical fan palm whose sap is fermented into palm wine, called toddy

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a pun: the Syrian city's name splits as PAL (friend) and MYRA (a girl). The second is the palm tree tapped for toddy.
explanation.definitionFit: The palmyra palm of South Asia is tapped for sap that ferments into toddy, and it shares its name with the Syrian city.

clue.text: Local monarch next to magpie

parts.note: a local is a pub, an inn
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A village pub, the queen and a magpie sit side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: On an archery or rifle target the rings run bull, inner, magpie, outer, so the ring beside the magpie is this one.
explanation.definitionFit: In target shooting the magpie ring lies just outside the ring next to the bull, so that ring is adjacent to it.

clue.text: Church interrupting an irreverent boy

indicators.note: the church abbreviation breaks into the middle of the word for irreverent

parts.note: ribald means coarsely irreverent or bawdy

explanation.surface: A churchman breaks in on a cheeky lad's rude remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Archibald is a male first name, so it stands for a boy.

clue.text: A desire to get a letter

parts.note: an itch is a restless desire for something

explanation.surface: Wanting badly to receive some post.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, H.

clue.text: Maybe reckon about 50-50 one's not wearing a tie

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the pair of fifties
maybe suggests the word that follows is one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties give LL

explanation.surface: I'd guess it's an even chance that someone turns up without a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' and 'about' look like loose filler in the sentence, but one signals the mixing and the other the wrapping; 50-50 stands for two Roman fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollneck is a high-collared sweater that covers the throat, worn instead of a shirt and necktie.

clue.text: Strength and loyalty saw slatterns put straight

indicators.note: putting things straight means sorting them out, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone saw untidy women set right with firmness and devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwartness combines sturdiness with steadfast loyalty, matching both halves of the phrase.

clue.text: Thinning out bureaucracy as indexed?

indicators.note: an index lists a phrase under its main noun, putting the adjective after a comma, so the first word moves to the end

parts.note: red tape is the standard idiom for bureaucracy

explanation.surface: Is administrative paperwork shrinking, as the index suggests?
explanation.walkthrough: In an index red tape appears as 'tape, red', which reads as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows gradually towards one end, becoming thinner.

clue.text: Partisan in 27 reported solver's bust

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the words heard are written as a sound-alike

parts.note: what belongs to the solver is yours; a bust is a chest, which in Scots is a kist

explanation.surface: A supporter in a historic war is said to have broken the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: KIST is a Scots word for a chest; 'your kist' said aloud gives the answer. 27 is the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkists were supporters of the House of York, one side in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Tito's hunchbacks

definitions.meaning: the surname of Tito, the celebrated Italian operatic baritone
the Italian plural noun for people with a humped back

explanation.walkthrough: Tito is not the Yugoslav leader but the Italian baritone, whose surname is also Italian for hunchbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The baritone was Tito Gobbi, and gobbi is the Italian plural of gobbo, a hunchback.

clue.text: A French nobleman turned up on Hebridean island to fish

indicators.note: in a down clue the turned piece sits on the island in the sense of following it

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides off Scotland

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a duc is a French duke

explanation.surface: A French duke goes up to a Scottish island to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' in a down clue makes the French duke and the A read upwards, so they sit beneath the island when entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A barracuda is a large predatory sea fish with fearsome teeth.

clue.text: Rhyming letters? I would say not: it's hermaphrodite

definitions.text: Rhyming letters? I would say not: it's hermaphrodite

parts.words: Rhyming letters? I would say not: it's hermaphrodite
parts.note: the slow post is a rhyming phrase for letters; and the creature named in it is not a male, since it is hermaphrodite

explanation.surface: A rhyme about letters, and a denial that the creature involved is male.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase rhymes, means letters sent by post, and puns on 'snail male': the setter says not, as snails are hermaphrodite.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow traditional post is nicknamed after the sluggish garden mollusc, contrasted with email.

clue.text: Actors in a way on right side in 27

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is attached on to the end
the actors sit in the way, inside the word for a way

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road, a way
a cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Actors take a road on the right side of a historic war.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is the Wars of the Roses; Lancaster was the red-rose side.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster was one of the two rival factions in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Go with a winner to make wood for Beatles

indicators.note: these letters are worked up to make something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Back a winner to get timber for a pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norwegian Wood' is a Beatles song, so the answer is the Beatles' kind of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title 'Norwegian Wood' names the wood the Beatles sang about.

clue.text: Distance that is key to being high up on shield

parts.note: an inch is a small distance
i.e., id est, means that is
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: A small gap is crucial to staying high on a defender's shield.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry the chief is the top band of a shield; a charge placed there is said to be in chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic usage puts a charge in the chief, the top third of the shield, so it sits high up.

clue.text: Absolutely unequal to cancelling game?

definitions.meaning: hopelessly outclassed by someone, as in the idiom for being far inferior
a fixture called off, so there is no game today

explanation.definitionFit: Being no match for someone means being far inferior; read literally the phrase says a fixture is off.

clue.text: Name of girl in the CPR

indicators.note: the girl's name sits inside the full name the initials stand for, so everything around it is dropped

parts.note: CPR stands for the Canadian Pacific Railway

explanation.surface: A girl's name appears on the Canadian railway.
explanation.walkthrough: Expand CPR to Canadian Pacific Railway; dropping the letters around it leaves the name inside 'Canadian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a female first name of Slavic origin, meaning hope.

clue.text: Deal with cars etc

definitions.meaning: to trade or do business with, often illicitly

explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to trade, often illegally, and the noun means the stream of road vehicles.

clue.text: Novel river with candy

definitions.meaning: the river in George Eliot's novel The Mill on the ...
the spun-sugar sweet sold at fairs pairs this word with candy

explanation.walkthrough: The river runs through George Eliot's novel of St Ogg's; candy ... is spun-sugar fairground fluff.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's Mill stands on this river, and candy floss is the fairground spun-sugar sweet.

clue.text: Maximum base to give setter a home

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: The greatest base is there to give the crossword compiler somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' is the adjective meaning low or vile, so 'Maximum base' means most contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low or ignoble; the superlative of mean in that sense is the most contemptible.

clue.text: First off numbers 50-50

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for numbers is taken off

parts.note: sevens are numbers

explanation.surface: The opening numbers are an even bet.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, odds of even money mean a fifty-fifty chance.

clue.text: Pollster's in building with joker

indicators.note: the pollster's name goes inside the word for a building

parts.note: a hut is a small building
MORI is a British polling company; the possessive supplies the S

explanation.surface: A pollster's office is in the same building as a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: MORI is a well-known British opinion-poll firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorist is a writer or performer of comic material, a joker.

clue.text: Opposition to English subject

parts.note: the other side is them, as in us and them

explanation.surface: Resistance to the study of English as a school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Weak leading man's breaking goods in horticultural contests

indicators.note: the weak leading man breaks into the goods, splitting the word open

parts.note: wares are goods for sale
soft means weak
the leading man is the hero; the possessive gives HERO'S

explanation.surface: A feeble star actor smashes produce at a flower show.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke: the fifteenth-century civil wars, fought by houses with rose badges, are cast as gardening contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Battles between the white and red rose houses are jokingly pictured as rose-growing competitions.
